spatial_claims.claim: C is a point on line segment AB (BC subtracted from AB)

configuration_map: The only geometric configuration is a straight line AB with a point C on it, dividing it into segments AC and BC. No auxiliary points, triangles, circles, angles, or other geometric figures are constructed. All reasoning operates on areas (squares and rectangles) and their commensurability properties (rational, medial, irrational classification).
skip_reason: Purely algebraic proof about classification of irrational magnitudes. The proof uses an algebraic identity (Prop 2.7) and commensurability properties (10.12, 10.15, 10.26) to show that the square on AC is neither rational nor medial. No geometric configuration claims beyond the trivial setup of a point on a line segment. No angle decompositions, no inside/outside claims, no ray orderings, no circle arguments.
